counterargs.read: Today's yield backup looks more like a real-rate/growth-repricing move than an inflation scare — breakevens didn't move and credit actually tightened, while bond vol eased sharply. But oil's three-session +3.77% rise is the wildcard: if it starts showing up in breakevens ahead of Wednesday's CPI print, the read shifts toward inflation-reacceleration. The Korea gate closing back to 1/3 (EWY re-failing its SMA20) is a reminder that Friday's brief 2/3 open was fragile, not a trend change.

trade_table.rationale: Curve backed up +4-6bp across the board today; TLT -0.43% confirms the move. Real yields (DFII5 +2bp) doing the work, not inflation — still a headwind for duration into CPI Wednesday.
SOXX -0.80% today but +1.21% over 3 sessions; SOXX/SPY ratio ticked up to 0.698 from 0.693 — structurally still holding despite the pullback.
Gate closed back to 1/3 — EWY fell back below its 20-day SMA (162.62 vs 164.33) after Friday's brief flip; KOSPI still ~23% below its 8,200 threshold.
HY OAS tightened 4bp to 2.71%, lender proxies (ALLY/CACC/COF) broadly stable-to-firmer — no stress, improving on the margin.
CL1! +3.77% over 3 sessions — hasn't shown up in breakevens yet, but a hot CPI print Wednesday paired with this move would flip the inflation-reaccel case on.

catalysts.note: ~46h out; key test given oil's 3-session +3.77% run and real yields (DFII5/10) drifting up 2bp — a hot print would confirm inflation-reacceleration, a soft one would support the growth-repricing read.
